Rhodium-Catalyzed C-H Functionalization-Based Approach to Eight-
membered Lactams 
Shangze Wu,a Rong Zeng ,a Chunling Fu, a Yihua Yu, c Xue Zhang, *b  and Shengming Ma *a,b 
Received (in XXX, XXX) Xth XXXXXXXXX 20XX, Accepted Xth XXXXXXXXX 20XX 
DOI: 10.1039/b000000x 5 
A Rh(III) catalyzed formal [4+2+2] cyclization of Ngpivaloyloxy benzamides 1 with 1,6gallenegenes 2 by 
CgH functionalization is reported. The reactions occur at room temperature and are compatible with air 
and moisture with a tolerance of many synthetically useful functional groups. The followgup 
modifications of the products have been demonstrated. After careful mechanistic studies and DFT 
calculation, a reaction mechanism was proposed.  10 
Introduction 
It is well known that mediumgsized rings are hard t o synthesize 
due to entropic and enthalpic reasons. 1 Among them, eightg
membered lactams are found in many natural products  and 
bioactive molecules. 2 The normal approach to these molecules 15 
often require harsh conditions (such as high temper atures and 
highly diluted solutions), at least stoichiometric amount of metal 
reagents, or pregfunctionalized starting materials by several 
steps. 3 Therefore, developing a catalytic procedure for th e 
efficient synthesis of eightgmembered lactams under  mild 20 
conditions is still desired. 
In principle, [2+2+2+2] or [4+2+2] cyclization woul d be the 
most straightforward yet challenging approach to th e eightg
membered lactams. 4 On the other hand, in recent years, directed 
Rh(III)gcatalyzed CgH functionalization reactions h ave been 25 
extensively studied. 5 Among them, the formal [4+2]gcyclization 
between arenes or alkenes with a proper directing g roup and 
unsaturated compounds such as alkenes, alkynes or a llenes 
facilely affording sixgmembered products have been well 
established. 6g12  We envisioned a strategy for the efficient 30 
construction of eightgmembered rings if a [2+2]gatom component, 
i.e., a molecule contains two unsaturated carbongcarbon bonds, is 
applied instead of alkenes, alkynes or allenes. The  challenge is 
the highly unfavorable selectivity for the formatio n eightg
membered ring since it is much easier to form sixgm embered 35 
rings (A’ vs. B) with the participation of just one  CgC πgbond 
(Scheme 1). Herein, we wish to report the realizati on of such a 
concept by applying an allenegene as the [2+2]gatom  component 
catalyzed by [Cp*RhCl 2]2 with Ngpivaloyloxy benzamides as the 
[4]gatom component under very mild conditions. 40 
 
Scheme 1 Rh(III)gcatalyzed cyclization: [4+2] vs [4+2+2] 
Results and Discussion 
After some trial and error with compounds bearing a t least two 
unsaturated CgC bond, we identified such a reaction , in which 3g45 
(trimethylsilyl)g1,2,6gheptatriene 2a  acts as a [2+2]gatom 
component while Ngpivaloyloxybenzamide 1a  behaves as the [4]g
atom component. When 1a  was treated with 2a  in a mixed 
solvent of MeOH and water (v/v 20/1) under the cata lysis of 
[Cp*RhCl 2]2, the expected [4+2+2] cyclization product, i.e., t he 50 
benzogfused eightgmembered lactam 3a , was indeed formed in 
75% NMR yield although together with the [4+2] regi oisomeric 
mixture 13  of two products 4aa  and 5aa  with the isolated carbong
carbon double bond being reacted as the minor products (Table 1, 
Entry 1). The structure of 3a  was confirmed by Xgray diffraction 55 
study (Scheme 2), 14  indicating that the allene unit has been 
reacted first. After screening the solvent, we foun d that MeOH 
was the best (Table 1, Entries 1g5). Moisture, air and 4Å MS had 
very little influence on the yield (Table 1, Entrie s 6g7). Then, the 
base effect was investigated and 30 mol% of K 2CO 3 was found to 60 
be the optimal (Table 1, Entries 2 and 8g13). Control experiments 
showed that no reaction occurred in the absence of [Cp*RhCl 2]2 
or bases. Finally, the reaction of 1a  and 2a  in methanol under the 
catalysis of [Cp*RhCl 2]2 with 30 mol% K 2CO 3 as base at room 
temperature was chosen as the optimal reaction cond itions for 65 
further study (Table 1, Entry 11).

βgH elimination from IN6 , are also be investigated. The energetic 65 
profiles for possible reactions from IN6  are presented in Figure 2.

membered rhodacycle IN6  should first isomerize to the more 
stable intermediate IN7  (11.7 kcal/mol lower in energy than IN6 ), 
in which the Rh center coordinates with the termina l CgC double 70 
bond instead of the carbonyl moiety in IN6 . Then the subsequent 
insertion of the terminal CgC double bond into the RhgC bond 
occurs via TS4  with an activation barrier of 9.1 kcal/mol. This

The activation free energy of direct reductive elim ination from 
IN6  is computed to be 35.5 kcal/mol ( TS5 , Figure 2), indicating 5

Based on the mechanistic investigations of a closel y related 
systems, 22 a more kinetically favorable pathway of CgN 
formation from IN6  is discovered through a high oxidation state 
Rh(V) nitrene species IN9 ,23 generated by the migration of the 10 
acetoxy moiety form N to Rh via a fivegmembered transition state 
(TS6 , Figure 2). This migration step is computed to be slightly 
endergonic ( ∆Gsol  = 6.8 kcal/mol) and requires a 13.8 kcal/mol 
activation barrier ( TS6 ). The nitrene Rh(V) species IN9  has a 
Rh=N distance of only 1.867 Å, which is much shorte r than the 15 
RhgN single bond distance of 2.162 Å in IN8 . The following 
reductive elimination of nitrene Rh(V) species IN9  is much easier 
with a barrier of only 7.7 kcal/mol via TS7 , affording IN10  
irreversibly with high exergonicity. Overall, the activation energy 
for the CgN bond formation pathway from IN6  is 14.5 kcal/mol, 20 
as defined by the energy gap between TS7  and IN6 .

We concluded that the key factor of the influence o f the NgOR 
moiety on the reaction selectivity could be attribu ted to the extra 5 
coordination of the carbonyl oxygen in the Ngacetoxy moiety 
with the Rh center in IN8 . First of all, this extra coordination in 
IN8  facilitates the migration of the acyloxy from N to  Rh, thus 
enable the formation of the high oxidation state Rh (V) nitrene 
intermediate IN14  (Figure 3), which is the CgN bond formation 10 
precursor. Secondly, the extra stabilization of IN8  by this kind of 
coordination increases the barrier of the whole βgH elimination 
process in the Ngacetoxy containing system, avoiding the 
formation of the 7gtype mthylenecyclopentene product. 
Conclusions 15 
In conclusion, we have developed the first [Cp*RhCl 2]2g
catalyzed [4+2+2] cyclization between Ngpivaloyloxy 
benzamides and 1,6gallenegenes forming eightgmembered lactams. 
These reactions proceed at room temperature and are  compatible 
with ambient air and moisture. Many arenes and alle negenes with 20 
many synthetically useful functional groups are compatible in the 
reactions. After careful mechanistic studies and DF T calculation, 
the reaction mechanism was presented in deatail and  the role of 
the NgOR moiety on the selectivity for the formation of the final 
products is also unveiled. The formed lactams have been 25 
transformed to cyclic vinylic iodide or desilylated product as well 
as the analogue of dopamine D 3 receptor. With easy availability 
of both starting materials and new concept to facil ely synthesize 
the 8gmembered rings, which are otherwise hard to c onstruct by 
other means, this [4+2+2] cyclization protocol will  be of high 30 
interest in organic chemistry and related disciplin es. Further 
studies involving three or more components and chir al [4+2+2] 
reaction are being carried out in our laboratory.
